body.statement: Theorem 3. For \(J=2\) and \(s=1\), the rational certificate \((q^{\mathrm U},\eta^{\mathrm U},\pi^{\mathrm H})\) satisfies \(q^{\mathrm U}\notin\mathcal C_2\) and \[\max_{h\in\mathcal H_{2,1}}\mathcal R_h(q^{\mathrm U},\eta^{\mathrm U})<9065/100000.\] Its displayed dual prior satisfies \[\min\left\{B_{(0,0,2)}(\pi^{\mathrm H}),\sum_{n\in\mathcal N_2}q^{\mathrm{Ber}}_nB_n(\pi^{\mathrm H})\right\}>9102/100000,\] and therefore \(\inf_{q'\in\mathcal C_2,\,\eta'}\max_h\mathcal R_h(q',\eta')>0.09102\). Hence \(\mathcal Q^*(2,1)\cap\mathcal C_2=\varnothing\), with an all-estimator risk gap exceeding \(37/100000\).
body.justification: The exact active-histogram witness shows that the strict separation is not produced by vanishing assignment support, a prior-null schedule region, a single accidental observation, or a constant estimator. It rules out only the paper-defined workflow that mixes paired assignment with the Bernoulli/nonlinear unrestricted prescription while reoptimizing every measurable clipped estimator.
body.gap: No cited paper is claimed to advocate the canonical mixture segment. The contribution is the internally defined all-estimator comparison and its exact rational, nondegenerate certificate under the hard \(J=2,s=1\) pair-discordance class.
body.consumer: For sensitivity analysis at \(J=2,s=1\), the result shows that restricting attention to the paper-defined paired--Bernoulli mixture workflow can be strictly suboptimal even after estimator reoptimization, with a certified gap exceeding \(37/100000\).
body.proof_tex:
Use the deterministic ordering in \(\texttt{def:j2-rational-certificate}\), with indices beginning at zero. The six assignment-orbit sizes are
\[
 (C_n)_n=(4,4,1,4,2,1),
\]
and the Bernoulli orbit masses are
\[
 (q_n^{\mathrm{Ber}})_n=(1/4,1/4,1/16,1/4,1/8,1/16).
\]
All displayed coordinates of \(q^{\mathrm U}\), \(\pi^{\mathrm U}\), and \(\pi^{\mathrm H}\) are nonnegative, and direct integer summation gives respectively \(100\), \(10^8\), and \(10^8\); hence they are probability vectors. If
\[
 q^{\mathrm U}=\lambda q^{\mathrm{pair}}+(1-\lambda)q^{\mathrm{Ber}},
\]
then the last coordinate gives \((1-\lambda)/16=1/100\), or \(1-\lambda=4/25\). The second coordinate would then be \((1-\lambda)/4=1/25\), but the second coordinate of \(q^{\mathrm U}\) is \(3/10\). Thus \(q^{\mathrm U}\notin\mathcal C_2\).

We now perform the exact kernel check and record a nondegeneracy witness. Histogram \(20\) consists of local schedule types \(3\) and \(7\), namely
\[
 t_3=\{(0,0),(1,1)\},
 \qquad
 t_7=\{(1,0),(1,0)\},
 \qquad
 h^{20}=e_{t_3}+e_{t_7}.
\]
It is feasible because each arm is discordant in exactly one pair, and
\[
 \tau_{h^{20}}=\frac{0+(-2)}4=-\frac12.
\]
The singleton region \(\{h^{20}\}\) has strictly positive mass under both certificate priors:
\[
 \pi^{\mathrm U}_{20}=\frac{16328392}{10^8}
 =\frac{2041049}{12500000}>0,
 \qquad
 \pi^{\mathrm H}_{20}=\frac{15653588}{10^8}
 =\frac{3913397}{25000000}>0.
\]

Uniformity inside assignment orbits and the displayed orbit sizes give, in the fixed six-orbit order,
\[
 \left(\frac{q_n^{\mathrm U}}{C_n}\right)_n
 =\left(\frac9{100},\frac3{40},\frac1{100},
 \frac3{40},\frac1{100},\frac1{100}\right).
\]
Thus every one of the \(16\) labelled assignments has probability at least \(1/100\). Applying the coefficient recurrence of Theorem 1 to the \(16\) local assignment strings for \(h^{20}\) gives twelve positive \((n,o)\) cells and the complete multisets
\[
 \{K_{20,no}:K_{20,no}>0\}
 =\{1^{(2)},(1/2)^{(6)},(1/4)^{(4)}\},
\]
\[
 \{q_n^{\mathrm U}K_{20,no}:K_{20,no}>0\}
 =\{(9/50)^{(2)},(3/20)^{(2)},(3/40)^{(4)},(1/100)^{(4)}\},
\]
where exponents denote multiplicities. The second multiset sums to one and proves the exact positive observation-orbit support bound
\[
 \min_{(n,o):K_{20,no}>0}q_n^{\mathrm U}K_{20,no}=\frac1{100}.
\]

For two explicit failure-driving cells, index the ten observed-pair types lexicographically and set
\[
 v_3=\{(0,0),(1,1)\},\qquad
 v_5=\{(0,1),(1,0)\},
\]
where each ordered pair is \((A,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\). Put
\[
 o^{(1)}=e_{v_3}+e_{v_5},\qquad o^{(2)}=2e_{v_5},
 \qquad n^{\mathrm m}=(0,0,2).
\]
The same recurrence, followed by the finite sums defining \(a\) and \(c\), gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
 o & K_{20,n^{\mathrm m},o}&a_{n^{\mathrm m}o}(\pi^{\mathrm U})
 &c_{n^{\mathrm m}o}(\pi^{\mathrm U})&\eta^{\mathrm U}_{n^{\mathrm m}o}\\ \hline
 o^{(1)}&1/2&6531357/40000000&1/400000000&1/65313570\\
 o^{(2)}&1/2&17288147/100000000&-13206049/100000000&-455381/596143
\end{array}
\]
Every denominator is positive. Since \(q_{n^{\mathrm m}}^{\mathrm U}=36/100\), each cell has probability \(9/50\) under \(q^{\mathrm U}K_{20}\). Their separate contributions to the risk at \(h^{20}\) are
\[
 \frac9{50}\left(\frac1{65313570}+\frac12\right)^2
 =\frac{266616417962449}{5924808925201250}>0,
\]
and
\[
 \frac9{50}\left(-\frac{455381}{596143}+\frac12\right)^2
 =\frac{890866036449}{71077295289800}>0.
\]
They also prove that the posterior-mean estimator is nonconstant on the observable experiment. Indeed, for any finite distribution with cell probabilities \(p_i\) and values \(z_i\),
\(
 \operatorname{Var}(Z)=\sum_{i<j}p_ip_j(z_i-z_j)^2
\).
Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{q^{\mathrm U}K_{20}}(\eta^{\mathrm U}_{NO})
 \ge \frac{81}{2500}
 \left(\frac{29742559416313}{38936227560510}\right)^2>0.
\]
This establishes exact design support, positive prior mass, multiple positive risk cells, and nonzero observable estimator variance at the active histogram.

For completeness, evaluating
\[
 \mathcal R_h(q^{\mathrm U},\eta^{\mathrm U})
 =\sum_{n,o}q_n^{\mathrm U}\frac{M_h(n,o)}{C_n}
 \left\{\frac{c_{no}(\pi^{\mathrm U})}{a_{no}(\pi^{\mathrm U})}-\tau_h\right\}^2,
\]
with zero on cells for which \(a_{no}(\pi^{\mathrm U})=0\), over all \(38\) feasible histograms gives
\[
 \max_{h\in\mathcal H_{2,1}}\mathcal R_h(q^{\mathrm U},\eta^{\mathrm U})
 =\mathcal R_{h^{20}}(q^{\mathrm U},\eta^{\mathrm U})
 =\frac{3850693539551962000276103702569949405421799518612146614194263925096941}
 {42480492487647577202373742417068406183238423509974554343379909221067500}.
\]
Exact subtraction yields
\[
 \frac{9065}{100000}-\mathcal R_{h^{20}}(q^{\mathrm U},\eta^{\mathrm U})
 =\frac{1304835626326984952608380298412920710108580536373896264998766342623}
 {339843939901180617618989939336547249465907388079796434747039273768540000}>0.
\]

The same coefficient table and \(\texttt{def:conditional-bayes-risk}\) give
\[
 B_{(0,0,2)}(\pi^{\mathrm H})
 =\frac{1120490298829500754077}{12309527381808500000000},
\]
and
\[
 \sum_{n\in\mathcal N_2}q_n^{\mathrm{Ber}}B_n(\pi^{\mathrm H})
 =\frac{1760496146710770175939617592960855471947446378734932636964736609}
 {19340529328385758315873504820452091980056895966176036468000000000}.
\]
Their respective exact excesses over \(9102/100000\) are
\[
 \frac{77116537291084077}{12309527381808500000000}>0
\]
and
\[
 \frac{121167241098454028811184203306059922667707893589797647376609}
 {19340529328385758315873504820452091980056895966176036468000000000}>0.
\]

Finally, consider only the paper-defined endpoint-mixture workflow
\[
 q_\lambda=\lambda q^{\mathrm{pair}}+(1-\lambda)q^{\mathrm{Ber}},
 \qquad 0\le\lambda\le1,
\]
while allowing its estimator to be reoptimized over all measurable clipped rules. This is an internal benchmark; no cited paper is asserted to advocate this mixture. For every \(\eta\), maximum risk dominates Bayes risk under \(\pi^{\mathrm H}\), and the cellwise posterior-mean calculation in Theorem 1 gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \max_h\mathcal R_h(q_\lambda,\eta)
 &\ge \inf_{\eta'}\sum_h\pi_h^{\mathrm H}
 \mathcal R_h(q_\lambda,\eta')\\
 &=\lambda B_{(0,0,2)}(\pi^{\mathrm H})
 +(1-\lambda)\sum_nq_n^{\mathrm{Ber}}B_n(\pi^{\mathrm H})\\
 &>\frac{9102}{100000}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The two endpoint excesses displayed above have a strictly positive minimum, so the strict inequality remains uniform after taking the infimum over \(\lambda\) and \(\eta\). On the other hand, the unrestricted minimax risk is at most the certified risk of \((q^{\mathrm U},\eta^{\mathrm U})\), which is below \(9065/100000\). Therefore \(\mathcal Q^*(2,1)\cap\mathcal C_2=\varnothing\), and the all-estimator gap is strictly larger than
\[
 \frac{9102-9065}{100000}=\frac{37}{100000}.
\]
